title: 15 U.S.C. § 77k — Civil liabilities on account of false registration statement (Securities Act of 1933 § 11), subsections (b)(3) and (c)
authors_or_organization: U.S. Congress (text via Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School)
limitations: Statutory text only: states the legal standard for the due diligence and reliance defenses; does not show how courts apply it, how much investigation is performed in practice, or what it costs. Secondary host (LII) rather than official U.S. Code site; text checked against quotations in R3B-S03 and R3B-S04.

title: 17 CFR § 230.176 — Circumstances affecting the determination of what constitutes reasonable investigation and reasonable grounds for belief under section 11 of the Securities Act
limitations: Lists non-exclusive circumstances only; specifies no procedures, effort level, or safe harbor. The 1998 proposal to add specific practices (incl. comfort letters) was never finalized (per R3B-S04).

title: Escott v. BarChris Construction Corp., 283 F. Supp. 643 (S.D.N.Y. 1968)
authors_or_organization: U.S. District Court, S.D.N.Y. (McLean, J.); text via Harvard Law School Caselaw Access Project
data_collection_dates: Facts concern the May 1961 debenture registration statement
limitations: Single trial-court decision on 1961 facts (findings after trial). Establishes what one court held sufficient/insufficient for named defendants; not a measure of general practice or of effort levels. CAP text lacks reporter page numbers in extracted form; locators use the opinion's own section headings.

title: In re WorldCom, Inc. Securities Litigation, 346 F. Supp. 2d 628 (S.D.N.Y. 2004) — Opinion on underwriter defendants' and lead plaintiff's summary judgment motions
authors_or_organization: U.S. District Court, S.D.N.Y. (Cote, J.); text via Harvard Law School Caselaw Access Project
data_collection_dates: Facts concern WorldCom bond offerings of May 2000 and May 2001
limitations: Summary-judgment ruling (no trial findings; underwriters later settled). Holdings are about what a jury could find; descriptions of underwriters' actual diligence are the parties' contentions. District-court decision, persuasive not binding outside S.D.N.Y. Locators use the opinion's section headings.

title: AS 6101: Letters for Underwriters and Certain Other Requesting Parties (in PCAOB Auditing Standards, for fiscal years beginning on or after 12/15/2024, compiled PDF pp. 555ff.)
publication_date: Compiled edition effective for fiscal years beginning on or after 2024-12-15
limitations: Professional standard: shows obligations and the profession's stated rationale, not what underwriters actually do with comfort letters, how much they re-check, or compliance. Only the AS 6101 portion of the compiled PDF was reviewed (paras .01-.47 and parts of the appendix). Proposed 2026 amendments (R3B-S06) not reflected.

title: PCAOB proposes to eliminate 135-day outside date for negative assurance in comfort letters (Client Update)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Law firm whose capital-markets practice advises underwriters and issuers; states it filed a comment letter on the related SEC semiannual reporting proposal and calls the PCAOB proposal 'a welcome change'.
limitations: Practitioner characterization of market practice ('usually unwilling') without data; the underlying PCAOB Release No. 2026-008 and docket (pcaobus.org) returned a bot-challenge page and were not reviewed directly. Proposal not adopted or SEC-approved as of access date.

title: Basis for Conclusions: International Standard on Related Services 4400 (Revised), Agreed-Upon Procedures Engagements
authors_or_organization: Staff of the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB/IFAC)
limitations: Basis for Conclusions summarizes respondents' comments and IAASB decisions; it is not the standard itself (the standard PDF at irba.co.za returned an HTML block page). Shows design rationale and stakeholder views, not measured user behavior or effort.

title: Brehm v. Eisner, 746 A.2d 244 (Del. 2000)
authors_or_organization: Delaware Supreme Court (Veasey, C.J.); text via Harvard Law School Caselaw Access Project
data_collection_dates: Facts concern Disney board's 1995 approval of the Ovitz employment agreement
limitations: Pleading-stage (Rule 23.1 demand futility) decision: sets out what a complaint must allege to rebut reliance; does not find facts about what the board did. Delaware fiduciary law (gross-negligence process standard) differs from negligence-based securities or lender standards. The §141(e) statutory text itself is already in the register.

title: Smith v. Van Gorkom, 488 A.2d 858 (Del. 1985)
authors_or_organization: Delaware Supreme Court (Horsey, J.); text via Harvard Law School Caselaw Access Project
data_collection_dates: Facts concern Trans Union board meeting of 1980-09-20
limitations: Single, much-criticized decision; Delaware later enacted §102(b)(7) exculpation (1986), limiting monetary liability for care breaches. Concerns reliance on an insider's oral presentation rather than an outside expert report; doctrine, not practice data.

title: Borrower/vendor due diligence – when it is not due (or diligent)
authors_or_organization: Clifford Chance LLP, Construction Insights blog (individual author not captured from page)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Law firm that acts as lenders'/purchasers' counsel and markets specialist construction diligence services (the post acknowledges 'blow our own trumpet').
limitations: Anecdotal practitioner opinion ('increasingly coming across'); no counts, sample, or effort data; author's firm benefits from lenders engaging their own counsel.

title: Homa Bay Biogas ONE Project, Kenya — Request for Proposal for a Lenders' Technical Advisor (Technical Due Diligence)
limitations: One lender's RfP for one renewable (biogas) project; shows an intended reliance allocation and scope, not what equity investors actually did with the report. Only the reliance clause and scope overview were reviewed (R3C covers IE scopes in depth).
